title: Access Recertification Run-through and Evidence Matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working note captures the run-through for the upcoming quarterly privileged access recertification, plus a compact evidence matrix we can use to automate proof collection for reviewers and auditors. Focus areas: RBAC v2 role mappings, audit log fields required for SIEM export, evidence snapshot commands, and a fallback process for manual attestations.

High-level goals (Q2 recert):
- Ensure all roles in RBAC v2 have an explicit owner and justification string in the directory.
- Produce machine-verifiable evidence artifacts for 90% of high-privilege accesses (console, API keys, service principals).
- Emit SIEM-ready audit exports with the schema below (field mapping + sample).
- Trial automated email nudges + one-click attestations via the internal console for managers.

Run sequence (recommended):
1) Pre-collection (T-7 days):
   - Freeze role changes (announce window).
   - Owner sweep: run `rbac-tool list-roles --orphaned` and assign temp owners for any orphaned role.
   - Publish recert schedule to #sec-recert channel and to owners list.
2) Automated evidence collection (T-3 to T-1 days):
   - Run `evidence-collector` job (kicked via CI) per team that emits: role-membership.csv, last-auth.csv, active-keys.csv, session-history.jsonl (sample), and compact policy-deltas.txt.
   - Jobs push artifacts to internal secure storage with signed URLs and immutability flags.
3) Manager review window (T+0 to T+7):
   - Managers receive one-click attest link. UI shows: role, members, last_active, attached tickets, suggested revocations (from policy engine).
   - Actions: attest / request removal / escalate to security.
4) Evidence retention and audit packaging (T+8):
   - For attested items, lock evidence set and produce a package with audit manifest (sha256 checksums).
   - Export to SIEM via bulk export job for cross-correlation with AD/Okta and infra logs.

Evidence matrix (fields we should collect and how to prove):
- role_id: RBAC v2 canonical id (rbac-tool output) — proof: role-membership.csv (signed)
- role_name: human-friendly name — proof: policy-delta + doc link
- role_owner: owner email — proof: owner assignment record (audit log event id)
- members: list of principal ids (users/service-ids/groups) — proof: role-membership.csv + last-auth.csv
- last_active: ISO timestamp of last authenticated action — proof: last-auth.csv + session-history.jsonl
- active_keys: count and fingerprints for keys associated with principals — proof: active-keys.csv and key-rotate tickets
- temporary_exceptions: list of granted exceptions (with expiry) — proof: exception-policy audit entries
- justification: short text attached to role (why exists) — proof: role metadata field + Confluence link if present

Minimum SIEM export schema (required fields for downstream auditors):
- tenant_id (string)
- event_time (ISO8601)
- event_type (ACCESS_GRANTED | ACCESS_REVOKED | ROLE_UPDATED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | KEY_CREATED | KEY_REVOKED)
- actor (principal id/email)
- target (role_id or key_fingerprint)
- target_type (role | key | user | service_account)
- reason (free text)
- evidence_url (signed URL)
- audit_id (unique event id)
- checksum (sha256 of attached evidence package)

Notes on audit log schema mapping (RBAC v2 -> SIEM):
- RBAC v2 emits internal events with fields: ts, actor, action, object_type, object_id, delta, request_id. Map `ts` -> event_time, `action` -> event_type (normalize), `object_type` -> target_type, and include `request_id` as audit_id.
- Always attach `evidence_url` to events that modify role membership or owner. The evidence collector will produce signed, time-limited urls and add them to the event payload during export.
- For chunked exports (large recert sets), include `batch_id` in the SIEM export to allow reassembly.

Automation checklist (scripts and jobs):
- evidence-collector (CI job): collects RBAC membership, sessions, keys, exceptions. Output: tar.gz with manifest.jsonl.
- signer service: produces signed upload urls + immutability flag.
- siem-exporter: polls completed evidence packages and writes normalized events into the SIEM ingest topic (Kafka/http).
- notifier: emails managers and posts Slack summary with link to attestation UI.
- reconciliation job: detects inconsistencies between role-membership.csv and identity provider (Okta/AD) and flags or creates tickets SEC-312-like.

Sample commands (ad-hoc run):
- rbac-tool list-roles --format csv > role-membership.csv
- sessions-query --since=90d --format jsonl > session-history.jsonl
- key-inspect --all --format csv > active-keys.csv
- python tools/evidence_pack.py --inputs role-membership.csv session-history.jsonl active-keys.csv --out evidence-q2-2026.tar.gz

Risk & fallback modes:
- If evidence-collector fails for a team: escalate to manual collection (run the ad-hoc commands, capture screenshots of console actions, and create a ticket with the artifacts).
- If SIEM export hits a schema error: buffer the export and create a remediation ticket; include the exported payload as archived JSON and notify SRE on-call.

Outstanding questions (for the working group):
- How do we handle cross-tenant service accounts that are shared between projects? (policy suggestion: convert to tenant-scoped SA with proxy role).
- Threshold for automatic revocation suggestions: should we suggest revocation at 90 days of inactivity for dev roles and 30 days for infra and admin?
- Do we store evidence packages longer than 1 year for high-risk roles? Legal wants 7 years for some regulated customers.

Appendix A — suggested attestation UI fields (compact):
- Role name, owner (link), current members (count + link), last active (list top 5 principals by recency), suggested action (revoke/suspend/ok), attached tickets, evidence package link, comments textbox, attest button (+ optional 2-step MFA if role_class=critical).

Appendix B — example SIEM event (line JSON example):
{"tenant_id":"redwood-prod","event_time":"2026-03-05T18:12:22Z","event_type":"OWNER_ASSIGNED","actor":"noelle.ortiz@redwood.ai","target":"role:r_admins","target_type":"role","reason":"quarterly recert assignment","evidence_url":"https://storage.internal.redwood/signed/evidence-q2-2026.tar.gz?sig=xxxx","audit_id":"req_20260305_9f3b","checksum":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924..."}

Next steps (this doc):
- Quick review with Security PM (Ravi) and Product (Noelle) — capture feedback and lock schema by 2026-03-10.
- Create runner in CI: `sec/ci/evidence-collector` MR (assigned to Connor).
- Pilot with infra and platform-eng teams in the next cycle (Q2).

Notes-to-self / freeform:
- keep the evidence package small (under 50MB) for easier long-term storage — prefer CSV + jsonl + manifest rather than full logs.
- mark stream outputs as canonical and compress with zstd.
- consider adding immutable timestamping (notarization) for high-value packages.

References / links: see linked_artifacts for starting tickets and runbook.

---
End of working note.
